posts.body:
​
Introducing the third edition of A Celestial Weapon. I first made this in Rpg Maker 2003, then remade it in Rpg Maker MV, and now for a third time in Rpg Maker MZ. AI has only been used in producing the title screen for the game, as seen above. Graphics have been compiled from Microsoft Copilot, graphics from pixabay.com, the Rpg Maker MV RTP, and GIMP.
Synopsis
​
On a clear night, a meteor fell on the teritory of Soldaria, the authoritarian dictatorship run by the mysterious Mr. B and his small group of ministers.
​
Richards
, who only goes by his surname, who runs the Justice Department.
​
​
The beautiful (and with an ego to match it), General
Jodie Felchers
, the head of the military.
​
​
Dr. James Hawser
, the head of the Department of Science. An amoral scientist who's ethics are based on the "Just because I can" mindset.
​
​
Andrew Williams
, the head of the energy agency. He's the only one who was in the government prior to the "revolution" twenty years ago. The only member of the government who could be described as "decent", and is well loved by the people. They affectionately refer to him as "Uncle Williams".
​
​
And finally, the enigmatic
Mr. B.
None of the citizens know if he truly exists or not, if he's a real person or just a figurehead shown by the other four ministers.
​
​
​
The biggest thorn in their side is the resident skeptic of Canaburg, one simply known as Sophie. She and her friend James feel that this wasn't a meteorite which fell in their territory. A quick trip to the government building in the capital city of Canaburg tells Sophie all she needs to know, and soon she, her friends James and Vincent, Jared and Heather, and two others she's encountered along the way are heading to the nation of Senecia which lies across the sea to the north. General Felchers is planning on building a horrific weapon to use against them, and they can only hope the Senecian government will heed their warning before it's too late.

new images are shown here.
​
New ammo can now be crafted anytime, anywhere, as long as it's outside of battle. The long trip to Sagarisk is no longer necessary.
​
The new port at Senecia. Shown above is the attempt to show cargo ships at the dock.
Linda is questioned at the prison in Senecia.

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
changing actor sprite won't just glitch, make sure it's preloaded before hand
and have a butter (2-5 wait) between the image to change to max 15 as buffer.
if it's not there, the engine kinda skips the processing and load it next time
by opening/closing the menu for example.
another solution is a map refresh mode so it would changes on the map

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Well, I played the MV version for my Feedback Friday this week, but since you're cancelling it I guess I'll post it a bit early.
If it was a remake of the 2k3 version hopefully some of my comments will still help. I didn't run into any weird glitching with event appearances, though maybe that was all later in the game. Also, if you do want this thread closed, please make sure to report it.
I gave your demo a try but ended up stopping after meeting Jared. You've made a huge world that seems to have a lot of effort put into it, but I think the gameplay is making the entire thing suffer.
Spoiler:
Feedback
First thing I need to point out is that your use of AI is limiting your potential audience. Beyond the titlescreen which I didn't spend much time on, I never reached a point where there really was AI art so it's clearly not adding a lot to the game. The AI image you shared doesn't look good either, so I'm glad I didn't run into it while playing, but the fact is there are plenty of potential players who will not play your game because it's using AI. Do some thinking on if AI is really worth it to use.
Moving on to the game itself, the worldbuilding seems interesting but I think you need to keep in mind that players don't know everything that you as the dev know. Sophie gives some instructions on how to reach her home, but when it's time to visit Vincent's apartment he doesn't even mention which area of the city he lives in. I did eventually find it, and later on found out that the cell phone gave general directions, but the game could do a lot to introduce goals and key items to the player. There's a lot of backstory and comments about the world which is nice, but tweaking the dialogue to make sure players have a clear goal would be good.
Battles are another thing that needs more work. I was surprised when there was a sudden fight against the General since I had been thinking that the battle system would be introduced in a tutorial. Once the fight started, I was disappointed to find that nobody had any skills I could use in combat since that tells me that the game wants me to spam the default Attack in all future battles. I hoped that was wrong, but when I leveled up repeatedly and only James gained a combat skill I knew that combat hadn't been worked on enough. You don't need to give new skills every level up, but if you want players to really have fun in battles each character should have choices to make in battle. When there aren't any skills to choose from then you're asking players to just spam Attack which doesn't make for engaging combat. Even just giving everyone a single different starting skill would immensely help the battles not feel repetitive.
I saw that Jared had some skills when he joined, but by that point I wasn't having fun with the battles so I couldn't bring myself to keep playing.
There were a few other bugs and oddities:
The intro doesn't have a lot of fear shown when the sirens go off because each event moves one at a time. You can set it up so all the NPCs move towards the stairs at once, making it feel like they are at least a bit worried
Use tints! The bunker could be a dark, gloomy place where the citizens are talking, but at the moment it looks exactly the same as the outdoors so it doesn't feel like they're safe underground
The meeting with James is partly covered by the message box, be careful when setting up cutscenes so that the characters are easy to see near the middle of the screen. This could've been fixed by moving them up just one tile
This game hasn't had any chests when exploring, so having one with Sushi in it in the government workplace feels extra strange
The General says there are 4 militants in the buildings after being beaten, but there is only Sophie, James, and Vincent
There isn't a rush to escape after beating the General, most of the NPCs have the same lines and while there is an enemy wandering randomly, it's easy to get past them. This makes the whole situation feel like it's a joke and not serious
Power Cut doesn't 100% debuff enemy atk
Why does the male Soldier enemy give 100 exp and the female Soldier 50 exp?
Overall, you've clearly spent lots of time building up your game world and that shows. But the combat needs a lot more work to be able to match the level of the story and keep players interested.
Good luck with your future project!
